source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CloudHQ MCC2 sits in Prince William County, Virginia, one of the densest concentrations of data center infrastructure in the world. The operator's published specification for this campus lists 2,232,875 square feet of technical space. No IT load in megawatts, no critical power figure, and no redundancy tier is published on the operator's spec page, so this campus cannot be placed on the power-based ranking this site uses. Because no megawatt figure is published, it does not appear in Virginia's ranked list of 19 facilities with published capacity, and its rank of 20 in the state context reflects that absence, not a power measurement.

The square footage alone signals scale. At a conventional raised-floor density of roughly 150 watts per square foot of technical space, 2,232,875 square feet would imply something in the range of 335 MW of IT load, and at 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, that figure would correspond to roughly 8,375 racks. At a more modest 10 kW per rack, a colocation average, the same power estimate implies closer to 33,500 racks. These are illustrative calculations based on industry assumptions, not operator claims, and the actual figure depends entirely on how densely the space is fitted out, which is not published.

Virginia's 326 mapped facilities hold 1,326 MW of published capacity across the 19 sites that have disclosed a number. That average is roughly 70 MW per disclosing site. No certifications are listed in the published data for MCC2, so no statement about what workloads or compliance regimes the campus qualifies to host can be made. For a reader deciding whether this campus matters to AI, the footprint is large enough to matter if it is built out at modern densities, but the absence of a power figure means that conclusion rests on an assumption, not a published fact.
